newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali Islamic fighters reject Somalia formula.
newsitem.headline: Somali Islamic fighters reject Somalia formula.

text.p: The Islamic fundamentalist group al-Ittihad al-Islam, fighting Ethiopian troops who attacked its bases in southwestern Somalia last month, said it does not recognise the peace deal reached last week by Somali factions.
Military commander Colonel Hassan Dawir Aweys said on Sunday that al-Ittihad refused to recognise any agreement not based on Islam.

The 26 Somali faction leaders, after meeting in Ethiopia for the last two months, said on Friday they would set up a "National Salvation Council" authorized to establish a provisional central government.
But the agreement has other opponents as well.

Faction leader Hussein Aideed, who claims he is Somalia's president, boycotted the reconciliation meeting. Somalia has been without central authority since 1991 when rebels overthrew late president Mohammed Siad Barre.
In a separate weekend statement, al-Ittihad said 200 Somali civilians had been killed by Ethiopian troops in the latest fighting in western Somalia. Al-Ittihad killed 97 Ethiopian soldiers, it added.

It was the second time within four months that Ethiopian troops had attacked the bases of al-Ittihad -- which Ethiopia described as a "multinational terrorist group" -- in Somalia. But Ethiopia has made no statement on the latest incursion.
